title: Machine learning and genetic search predict stronger refractory alloys
summary: A random-forest model trained on published refractory high-entropy-alloy data was coupled to a stochastic genetic algorithm to optimize alloy compositions for yield strength at selected temperatures. For an AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr base composition, the authors report modeled gains of 90 MPa at 25 °C and 13% at 1,000 °C for optimized compositions. Other base-alloy optimizations are also reported. The proposed alloys were not experimentally fabricated or mechanically measured in this study; these are computational design predictions.
organization: CFD Research Corporation; University at Buffalo

evidence.tested: The model was validated against published experimental yield-strength data, including previously unseen datasets; the proposed optimized compositions and their target-temperature improvements were computational predictions.
evidence.unknown: The proposed optimized alloys were not experimentally fabricated or measured in this study; predicted yield strength depends on the source dataset and model assumptions.
evidence.ai_role: A random-forest model predicted yield strength and a stochastic genetic algorithm searched compositions to maximize strength at specified temperatures.
